**Practical SQL for Analysts – Context Note (Final Edition)**

---

**Decisions Made & What Was Chosen:**  
- **Teaching format:** Live, 6-week cohort with no slides — taught via live screen share in actual tools.  
- **Teaching style:** Jump-cut + floating query captions (e.g., 3-second talk → 10-second query → pause → fix).  
- **Platform:** No platform with buffering or poor global performance. Chosen: self-hosted, low-latency video delivery with direct control over encoding and CDN.  
- **Pricing:** One-time, no lifetime access. Tiers: $199 (Core), $299 (Plus), $499 (Pro).  
- **Community structure:** Private Discord + public forum. Students self-organize help; weekly 45-minute office hour (after Week 3).  
- **Capstone project (Compass):** Gated to Week 4 — unlocked after students complete Weeks 1–3.  
- **Sandbox usage:** Not designed for 200 students at once. Students use it in small bursts; no live concurrency required.  
- **Student data:** Full ownership of emails and payment relationships — for nurture, follow-up, and community.  
- **CE credit pathway:** Contact Wilhelmina Choo (analyst association) for future accreditation.  

**Key Terms & Definitions:**  
- **Jump-cut + floating query:** Teaching style with tight 3–15 sec segments: talking head → query in editor → floating caption.  
- **Sandbox:** Shared database environment where students run practice queries — *not* the platform’s checkout sandbox.  
- **Compass project:** Capstone analysis of a messy, real-world dataset — delivered as 5–7 queries + narrative.  
- **Office hour:** One 45-minute session per week (after Week 3), student-led Q&A.  
- **No slides:** Zero slide decks — all teaching delivered via live screen share.  
- **No lifetime access:** All pricing is one-time, no recurring or perpetual access.  

**Constraints & Preferences:**  
- No slide-heavy lectures.  
- No platform with buffering in India/Brazil/India.  
- No lifetime access.  
- No auto-graded quizzes or platform tracking.  
- Students help each other — no 24/7 support.  

**Approaches Tried & Ruled Out:**  
- **Self-paced modules:** Ruled out — lower completion, no human touch.  
- **Drip-release (drip model):** Ruled out — lacks momentum, poor retention.  
- **Coursemint:** Ruled out — buffering in low-bandwidth regions, poor global performance.  
- **Slide-heavy lectures:** Ruled out — no alignment with analyst workflow.  
- **Open-ended, unstructured community:** Ruled out — no clear rhythm, high support load.  

**Next Steps:**  
- Finalize 6-week cohort calendar with weekly flow.  
- Record one full lesson using jump-cut + floating query style.  
- Test video on 3 devices (mobile, tablet, desktop) in different regions.  
- Launch landing page with one-click access.  
- Send first email to 50 beta testers with: *"I’m launching a 6-week live SQL course — no slides, no fluff, just real work. Join me in Week 1."*  
- Schedule first office hour (Week 4) on a fixed day/time.  
- Set up private Discord and public forum.  

**All decisions are final. No exceptions.**

- **Teaching Style**: Jump-cut + floating query captions. Tight, rhythmic, screen-locked. No slides. No decks. One talking-head segment (3–5 sec) followed by a query in the editor with floating caption. Students see real work, not theory.  
- **Cohort Structure**: 6 weeks, live, no slides, no fluff. One 45-minute office hour per week (after Week 3), on a fixed day/time.  
- **Platform**: No platform with buffering in India, Brazil, or Africa. Must support live screen share with low latency. No slide-heavy or auto-graded features. Only video, live, tool-based delivery.

- **Sandbox**: Students access via shared environment (e.g., DB Fiddle, BigQuery). No 200-student concurrent load required. Usage is low and staggered.

- **No Recurring Access**: No lifetime access. All pricing is one-time, value-based.

  - Live cohort over self-paced or drip release — higher completion, higher engagement.

  - No platform with buffering — Coursemint eliminated due to global performance failure.
